## Project context

- **Project:** Bonfire House, Chatham County, North Carolina; 2018 North Carolina Residential Code, adopting the 2015 IRC with amendments.
- **Building:** Two-story single-family dwelling with attached garage, crawlspace, decks and lap pool; drawings identify R-3 occupancy and Type V-B construction.
- **Climate zone:** 4A.
- **Drawings:** 34 sheets covering general information, architectural site planning, plans, elevations, sections, assemblies, details and schedules; survey intentionally removed, with no separate structural, civil, MEP, solar or pool engineering drawings provided.
- **Specifications:** Eleven-page, trade-organized booklet dated October 20, 2021, covering sitework, architectural materials, building systems, equipment and utilities; not organized into numbered CSI divisions.

## A. Internal consistency across sheets

A-1 | Cover sheet; A5.20 | The sheet list identifies deck sections as A5.11, but the actual deck-section sheet is A5.20. | Certain
A-2 | A7.02, elevation 5; A2.01B; A8.01 | Elevation 5 is titled “Guest Bathroom 19,” although the bathroom is Room 18 and Room 19 is the guest closet. | Certain
A-3 | A8.01, door 10-1; A2.01A; A2.02 | Door 10-1 appears in the door schedule without a corresponding tagged opening on the floor plans. | Certain
A-4 | G0.11; A2.01; A2.01B | The code summary declares four bedrooms, but the plans identify only three bedrooms and an office, leaving the fourth sleeping-room designation uncoordinated. | High
A-5 | G0.11, plumbing fixture count; A2.01A; A2.01B | The summary lists four lavatories, whereas the plans show two in the master bathroom and one in each of the other three bathrooms, totaling five. | Certain
A-6 | G0.11, plumbing fixture count; A2.01A | The summary lists one bathtub, whereas the plans show both a master bathtub and a bathtub in Bathroom 11. | Certain
A-7 | A8.01, Room 14; A2.01B; A4.01 | The powder-room finish schedule assigns F-4 carpet, contradicting the F-2 designation on its enlarged plan and placing carpet in a room shown with an overflow floor drain. | Certain
A-8 | A2.01B, enlarged Level 2 plan; A4.01 | The guest shower is tagged F-2 rather than the recessed, sloped shower assembly F-3. | Certain
A-9 | A8.01, Room 01; A7.01, elevations 6 and 7 | The entry-hall schedule assigns P-1 to the east wall and WD-1 to the west wall, while both interior elevations identify WD-4 paneling. | Certain
A-10 | A8.01, Room 10; A7.01, elevation 9; A7.10, detail 1 | The reading-nook wall finishes are scheduled as WD-1, while its elevations and section identify WD-4 tongue-and-groove wall surfaces. | Certain
A-11 | A7.01, elevation 1; A8.01, appliance schedule | The kitchen hood annotation calls it A3, although the appliance schedule assigns A3 to the oven and A5 to the hood. | Certain
A-12 | A3.01, east elevation; A2.02 | An upper window near the north end of the living-room east façade has an empty window-type diamond, preventing an unambiguous schedule reference. | High
A-13 | A3.01, west elevation; A4.01 | The connector roof is tagged R-2 in the west elevation, but the horizontal-assembly sheet defines only R-1. | Certain
A-14 | A4.01, R-1; A4.11, detail 4 | R-1 identifies a weather barrier below the roof rigid insulation, while detail 4 depicts weather barriers both above and below it, leaving the roof membrane scope inconsistent. | High
A-15 | A3.02, south elevation; A4.13, details 1 and 4 | The south reading-nook window references the bathroom-window jamb detail 4 rather than the reading-nook corner-window detail 1, without identifying the substitution as similar. | High

## B. Dimensional and geometric integrity

B-1 | A3.02, north elevation; A3.01; A3.10 | The north elevation labels the crawlspace datum 501'-0" while dimensioning it 6'-0" below Level 1 at 508'-0", whereas other sheets use 502'-0". | Certain
B-2 | A3.22, details 1 and 2 | Eighteen risers at the stated 6 11/16" total 120 3/8", exceeding the documented 10'-0" floor-to-floor rise by 3/8". | Certain
B-3 | A4.01, F-1 and F-3 | The listed layers of both F-1 and F-3 total 11" including the gypsum ceiling, rather than the indicated 10 1/2". | High
B-4 | A4.01, F-2 | The listed F-2 layers total 11 1/16" to 11 3/16" including gypsum, rather than the indicated 10 9/16", undermining the intended flush floor transitions. | High
B-5 | A4.00, E-2, E-3 and E-4 | Each framed exterior-wall assembly labels the rigid insulation 1 1/2" thick but dimensions that layer as 1". | Certain
B-6 | A4.00, E-3 | The dimensioned E-3 layers total 8 9/16", not the stated overall thickness of 8". | Certain
B-7 | A4.00, E-1; specifications p. 4 | The crawlspace insulation leader identifies 1/2" rigid insulation, while the assembly dimension and specification require 2". | Certain
B-8 | A2.01B, enlarged Level 1 north plan | The north-side dimension chain gives 22'-10" plus 11'-5", totaling 34'-3" rather than the stated 34'-4". | Certain
B-9 | A2.01A; A1.01 | The east entry ramp lacks a complete dimensional definition of its sloped run, start and finish elevations, and landing transitions. | High
B-10 | A5.01; A5.10; A5.30, detail 2 | The exterior stair system lacks a complete coordinated rise-and-run layout establishing tread depths, riser quantities and finished landing elevations for each flight. | High
B-11 | A1.01; A2.01; G0.11 | The building is shown relative to a 50-foot setback line without sufficient dimensioned ties to establish its construction location relative to the property boundaries. | High
B-12 | A3.01; A2.02 | Several clerestory openings are located vertically only by their graphics, without complete head or sill dimensions tied to a floor datum. | High

## C. Specification-to-drawing alignment

C-1 | A8.01, window schedule; specifications p. 3 | The window schedule specifies Marvin Ultrex products and Marvin model numbers, while the specifications require Andersen 400 Series windows. | Certain
C-2 | G0.11, project fenestration values; specifications p. 3 | The window specification requires code compliance but does not carry forward the tighter project U-factors and SHGC values listed in the code summary. | High
C-3 | A3.01–A3.03; A4.00; specifications pp. 2–3 | The specifications place wood cladding on south and west façades, while the elevations generally assign wood to east and south façades and fiber cement to north and west façades. | Certain
C-4 | A4.00, E-2; specifications p. 2 | E-2 uses 2×8 framing at the conditioned connector, contradicting the specification that all conditioned exterior walls are 2×6. | Certain
C-5 | A4.00, E-2, E-3 and E-4; specifications p. 4 | The drawings specify plywood sheathing with separate rigid insulation, while the specifications require insulated ZIP sheathing, without reconciling the products or assembly thicknesses. | Certain
C-6 | A4.01, floor assemblies; specifications p. 2 | The floor assemblies call for plywood subflooring, while the specifications require 3/4" Advantech tongue-and-groove panels. | Certain
C-7 | G0.11; specifications p. 4 | The ceiling specification states R-38 plus R-15 equals R-49, although the sum is R-53, which is also the value listed in the code summary. | Certain
C-8 | A8.01, door 03-1; A3.02; specifications p. 3 | Door 03-1 is scheduled as stained metal, drawn with glazing, and specified as a glazed Jeld-Wen wood door. | Certain
C-9 | A3.03, elevation 2; specifications p. 2 | The garage-door elevation shows solid horizontal panels without the long-panel windows required by the specified Clopay door. | High
C-10 | A2.01A; specifications p. 3 | The entry ramp is drawn as wet-laid SS-3 flagstone, but the concrete-work specification requires SS-2 limestone on concrete at the east porch and ramp. | Certain
C-11 | A7.01, elevation 2; specifications p. 5 | The WD-1 frame note extending to door 06-2 conflicts with the blanket requirement that door casing and trim be painted, without a stated natural-wood exception. | High
C-12 | A7.01, kitchen elevations; specifications p. 6 | The kitchen elevations call for a 6 mm SS-1 backsplash, while the selected Silestone backsplash thickness remains TBD in the specifications. | Certain
C-13 | A2.01A; A4.00, W-1; specifications p. 4 | The bedroom separation and specified Bathroom 11 acoustic partitions remain tagged as typical W-1 walls without the acoustic treatment required by the specifications. | Certain
C-14 | G0.11; A3.01–A3.03; specifications p. 7 | The drawings and code summary identify five exterior hydrants, while the plumbing specification identifies only three. | Certain
C-15 | A6.01, lighting schedule; specifications p. 8 | All 70 interior L1 downlights are scheduled as gimbal fixtures, while the specifications identify only 41 of the 70 as sloped recessed lights. | Certain
C-16 | A6.01; A2.01A; A2.01B; specifications p. 8 | L7 is scheduled as two fixtures despite multiple separate locations on the drawings and a specification quantity of 75 linear feet, with no coordinated run-length schedule. | Certain
C-17 | A6.01; specifications p. 9 | The ceiling plan repeatedly calls for CAT6E cabling, while the specifications require CAT6A. | Certain
C-18 | A2.01B; specifications p. 8 | The garage EV provision is called a 240 V, 60 A outlet on the plan but a hardwired charger connection in the specifications. | Certain
C-19 | A2.00; A5.01; specifications p. 10 | The drawings place pool equipment in the west-end extension, while the specifications place it on the side opposite the house toward the southwest end. | High
C-20 | A5.01; specifications p. 10 | The pool top-of-wall elevation and specified water-surface elevation are both 2'-0" below Level 1, leaving no stated freeboard between water and coping. | Certain
C-21 | A8.01, door 18-2; specifications pp. 9–10 | The guest shower door is scheduled with no frame, while the specifications require a semi-framed enclosure. | Certain
C-22 | A2.03; specifications pp. 1 and 11 | The documents describe a solar array with battery storage but conclude with a requirement only to make the house solar ready, leaving the contracted installation scope contradictory. | High
C-23 | A2.03; A4.13, detail 5; specifications p. 4 | The specified snap-lock metal-roof profile is not accompanied by confirmation of suitability or an alternate system for the drawn 2:12 connector and 1/4:12 canopy slopes. | Moderate
C-24 | G0.01, door-tag notes; specifications booklet | The drawings reference door data in Specifications Division 8, but the supplied booklet contains no numbered Division 8 or equivalent section cross-reference. | Certain
C-25 | Specifications p. 6; A7.10 | The custom bunk-nook specification references sheet A8.10, which is not included, rather than the reading-nook detail on A7.10. | Certain

## D. Building envelope and building science

D-1 | A4.01, R-1; A4.10, detail 7; A4.11, detail 4 | The roof details call for an air gap and vented soffits without establishing a connected intake-to-outlet ventilation path or identifying which roof cavities are intended to remain unvented. | High
D-2 | A4.10–A4.12; specifications p. 4 | The general air-sealing requirements are not translated into a continuous, identifiable air-barrier connection across wall tops, roof transitions and the connector junctions. | High
D-3 | A4.10, detail 8; A4.11, detail 2 | The window sill details do not establish a complete drained pan with back dam, end dams and a defined discharge path integrated with the wall weather barrier. | High
D-4 | A4.10, details 1, 2 and 4; A4.11, details 1–3 | The custom window and door frame details omit defined perimeter sealant joints and the separation between exterior rain seals and interior air seals. | High
D-5 | A4.00, E-1; A4.10, detail 6; A4.11, detail 5; specifications p. 2 | Below-grade CMU protection is described using parge coat and vapor-barrier terminology without identifying a suitable dampproofing or waterproofing system and its footing termination. | High
D-6 | A2.00; A3.20; specifications p. 2 | The specified reinforced crawlspace liner lacks detailed sealed transitions at foundation walls, piers, penetrations, the lowered floor area and the access doorway. | High
D-7 | A4.00, E-1; A4.11, detail 5; specifications p. 4 | The continuous crawlspace foam installation lacks an identified termite-inspection provision or an approved alternative appropriate to the North Carolina location. | Moderate
D-8 | A4.13, detail 5 | The porch-support steel penetrates the insulated exterior wall without a documented thermal break or a complete air-and-water seal around the penetration. | High
D-9 | A4.10, detail 3; A5.30, details 3 and 6 | Flush interior-to-exterior transitions are shown without a complete threshold pan and drainage arrangement demonstrating how water is kept out at the doors. | High
D-10 | A4.01, F-3 | The shower-floor assembly lists tile, bond coat, mortar, lath and plywood without a waterproof receptor membrane or its connection to the drain and surrounding walls. | Certain
D-11 | A4.00; A7.02; specifications pp. 4–5 | Shower walls, niches, seats and bathtub platforms are shown with tile finishes but no coordinated wet-area backing and waterproofing assemblies. | High
D-12 | A7.02, elevation 3; A4.11 | The instruction to waterproof tile at the Bathroom 11 window does not define a membrane-to-window connection or replace the typical wood-return detail with a complete wet-location assembly. | High
D-13 | A5.30, detail 1; specifications p. 2 | The tapered deck edge approaches the ground without a stated minimum wood-to-soil clearance or an under-deck drainage and ventilation provision. | High

## E. Code and life safety

E-1 | G0.11 | The allowable-height and area explanation relies on IBC Table 503 while the governing code is identified as the North Carolina Residential Code, without reconciling those design bases. | High
E-2 | A4.01, F-1 and F-2; A2.01B | The assemblies beneath habitable rooms above the garage specify ordinary 1/2" gypsum rather than documenting the required garage-to-habitable-room ceiling protection. | High
E-3 | A4.00, W-3; A3.10; A3.21 | The garage separation lacks coordinated wall-to-ceiling junction and opening-protection details establishing continuity of its protective lining. | High
E-4 | A8.01, doors 13-2 and 16-1 | Garage-to-house doors are scheduled as ordinary solid-core interior doors without qualifying thickness or fire-performance requirements and without identified self-closing or self-latching hardware. | High
E-5 | A2.01A; A2.01B; A8.01 | Sleeping-room emergency escape openings are not designated, and the nominal casement sizes are not supported by net-clear opening areas, clear dimensions and coordinated sill heights. | High
E-6 | A8.01; A2.01A; A3.22; A7.02 | The glazing schedule does not identify safety glazing at hazardous locations including tub and shower windows, glazing beside doors, and windows adjacent to stairs or landings. | High
E-7 | A3.22; A2.01B | The interior stair documentation does not establish minimum finished headroom or clear stair width after handrail projections. | High
E-8 | A3.22; A7.01, elevation 8 | The open stair conditions lack complete guard infill, opening-limit, graspability and handrail-return details. | High
E-9 | A2.01B; A3.22, detail 1 | The powder room beneath the stair lacks headroom dimensions demonstrating adequate clearance at the toilet and its required approach area. | High
E-10 | A5.10, elevation 4; A5.01 | The pool-access stair railing is labeled 26" high in the elevation, conflicting with the 36" plan annotation and warranting correction for handrail and guard requirements. | Certain
E-11 | A5.01; A5.10; specifications p. 3 | The cable pool-barrier design lacks documented opening limits, climbability criteria and ground clearances necessary to establish its suitability as a pool enclosure. | High
E-12 | A8.01, gates 22-1 and 22-2; A5.01 | The pool gates are specified only with generic gate-latch hardware, without self-closing requirements, protected latch location or coordinated opening direction. | High
E-13 | A2.01A; A5.01; specifications p. 10 | The master-bedroom door appears to provide direct access inside the pool enclosure, but the documents do not identify the required protection for dwelling openings forming part of that barrier. | High
E-14 | A7.10, detail 1 | The elevated sleeping nook has an 18" railing without establishing its treatment as a bunk or loft, its protective opening limits, or the guard height above the finished mattress. | Moderate
E-15 | A2.00; A4.00, E-1; specifications p. 4 | Crawlspace XPS is shown without a documented protective barrier or qualifying exposed-use listing despite the crawlspace being expressly designated for storage. | High

## F. Constructability

F-1 | A4.01, R-1; A4.11, detail 4; specifications p. 4 | The metal roof bears on 1×2 battens above insulation without specified batten spacing or continuous panel support demonstrating the required walkability. | High
F-2 | A4.01, R-1; specifications p. 4 | Galvalume roofing is placed over pressure-treated battens without a specified compatible separation layer or confirmation that the treatment is suitable for direct metal contact. | Moderate
F-3 | A4.01, F-2 | Tile and stone are shown thin-set directly over a single plywood layer without a backer, uncoupling layer or identified approved direct-bond installation system. | High
F-4 | A2.01A; A4.01, F-2; specifications p. 6 | The master-bathroom hydronic floor-heating requirement has no coordinated installation zone or assembly detail demonstrating how the flush floor elevation will be maintained. | High
F-5 | A4.11, details 1–3; specifications p. 2 | The projecting Accoya frames rely on an undefined frame-angle attachment without angle material, dimensions, fasteners or coordinated backing. | High
F-6 | A4.01, F-6; A4.10, detail 6; specifications p. 3 | Exterior stone paving lacks movement-joint and building-isolation details at concrete slabs, porch edges and wall interfaces. | High
F-7 | A5.01; A5.20, detail 1 | The flush stone-coping-to-wood-deck interface lacks a joint or separation detail accommodating differential movement and maintaining drainage. | High
F-8 | A7.02, elevations 6 and 9 | Master-bathroom grab bars are shown without concealed backing extents or anchorage details to be installed before wall closure. | High
F-9 | A2.00; A5.10; specifications p. 10 | The fenced pool-equipment enclosure beneath the deck lacks a dimensioned service opening or removable enclosure panel for equipment installation and replacement. | High
F-10 | A2.01B, office closet; A7.01, pantry shelving; specifications pp. 5 and 9 | Network mounting panels above six feet are not coordinated with the office-closet door head and upper pantry shelving, leaving their installation surfaces and access unresolved. | High
F-11 | A7.10, detail 1; specifications p. 6 | The custom elevated bed, ladder and railing are shown with “framing as needed” rather than buildable support, attachment and ladder-connection details. | High

## G. Completeness and clarity

G-1 | Specifications pp. 3, 5 and 10 | Items described as allowances, including the well, septic system and entry hardware, lack stated allowance amounts or a consistent pricing basis. | Certain
G-2 | Specifications p. 1; G0.11 | The requirement to build to HERO standards is not accompanied by a defined compliance, testing or acceptance process, while certification remains an owner option. | High
G-3 | Specifications pp. 2–6 | Exterior colors, stains, wood-floor product, carpet and cabinet hardware remain unresolved without a coordinated finish-selection schedule or defined bid substitutions. | Certain
G-4 | A6.01; specifications p. 8 | Lighting fixture manufacturers and models remain TBD, with insufficient product or allowance information to price the scheduled fixtures consistently. | Certain
G-5 | A7.01; A7.02; specifications p. 6 | Countertop thicknesses, edge profiles and support requirements are not established for the custom island and vanity configurations. | High
G-6 | A8.01; specifications pp. 3 and 5 | Most door hardware entries are blank, and the generic lever and entry-lock descriptions do not establish complete hardware sets or functions. | Certain
G-7 | A8.01; A2.01A; A2.01B | The door schedule lacks an operation/type designation and leaf breakdown for wider closet openings, including the 4-foot and 6-foot scheduled doors. | High
G-8 | A6.01; A8.01; A3.10 | Ceiling materials and finished heights or slopes are not comprehensively scheduled for the mix of sloped rooms, flat ceilings, closets and built-in areas. | High
G-9 | A8.01, Room 11; specifications pp. 4–5 | Wall finish T-1 is used in the room schedule without an explicit definition linking that tag to the selected tile products and their extent. | Certain
G-10 | A2.01A; specifications p. 3 | Dry-laid SS-3 patios and paths lack bedding, base, edge-restraint and transition details distinguishing them from the wet-laid stone work. | High
G-11 | A1.01 | The general site fence is shown without a defined height, material, construction detail or clear distinction from the pool-barrier scope. | High
G-12 | A1.01; specifications p. 1 | Granite driveway edging lacks unit dimensions, exposed height, foundation or bedding requirements and a typical installation section. | High
G-13 | A5.01; A5.20; specifications p. 10 | The instruction to finish exposed pool walls does not identify a finish material, backing system, termination or extent. | Certain
G-14 | A5.01; A5.20 | Pool coping is called a stone cap without a material designation, profile, thickness, attachment or waterproofing-interface detail. | High
G-15 | A4.01, R-1; A4.10; A4.11 | The roof member is called a “TJI wood open web joist,” conflating an I-joist with an open-web member while other details alternatively identify trusses or I-joists. | Certain
G-16 | A2.03; A4.11; A4.13 | The diagonal shed roofs lack a complete set of high-edge and rake closure details coordinated with the standing seams, soffits and wall cladding. | High
G-17 | Specifications p. 2; G0.01; A1.01; A3.01–A3.03 | The specifications state that elevations and topography are approximate, but the precise building datums are not tied to an identified construction benchmark or a coordinated set of proposed corner grades. | High
G-18 | A2.01A; A2.01B; specifications p. 7 | Overflow floor drains are drawn as required work, while the specification presents them as an unresolved owner question without establishing the final architectural containment and floor-treatment scope. | Certain
G-19 | Specifications p. 1 | Wisteria scraping, soil screening and debris disposal are described as desirable rather than clearly included, excluded or separately priced sitework. | High
G-20 | A5.01 | The removable pool-cover deck area lacks panelization, fastening, lifting and clearance details needed to make the indicated access usable. | High
G-21 | A4.13; specifications p. 3 | Fiber-cement corner trim is identified as “2×4” without a manufacturer or actual section dimensions, leaving the intended corner geometry and available product unresolved. | High

## Summary

The documents communicate the architectural design but leave numerous conflicts and construction interfaces unresolved for a bid set. The three greatest concerns are **garage, stair and pool life-safety documentation; envelope and wet-area waterproofing; and coordination of assemblies, schedules and specified products**. Dimensional discrepancies affect wall thicknesses, floor transitions and stair setting-out, while undefined selections and allowances create substantial pricing uncertainty. A coordinated revision should resolve these items before procurement, framing and enclosure work proceed.
